propers.name: Collect
propers.text:
Praesta, quaesumus, omnipotens Deus: ut, qui sanctorum Martyrum tuorum
Tiburtii, Valeriani et Maximi solemnia colimus; eorum etiam virtutes
imitemur. Per Dominum.

propers.name: Secret
propers.text:
Haec hostia, quaesumus, Domine, quam sanctorum Martyrum tuorum natalicia
recensentes offerimus: et vincula nostrae pravitatis absolvat, et tuae nobis
misericordiae dona conciliet. Per Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum, Filium
tuum: Qui tecum vivit et regnat.

provenance.provenance_evidence: The project-owned projection passage reproduces the retained calendar body hash exactly. Its artifact manifest records the bounded public-domain 1862 Pustet antecedent, the separate 1962 target, and every editorial transformation; neither witness is represented as owning the projected bytes. The 1962 reading was established on that edition's page images rather than its text layer, cross-read against the Benziger conformed printing. Differences from the antecedent: the 1862 carries `Postcommunio` here, which the CMAA text layer of the 1962 does not; the 1862 reads `d6bitse servi tutis` where the 1962 reads `I debitae servitutis`; the 1862 reads `senti mus augm6n tum` where the 1962 reads `sentiamus augmen j turn`; 3 further place(s) differ only in orthography, ligature or the recogniser's letterforms; the 1862 prints no conclusion at this place; the 1962 prints `Per Dominum nostrum Iesum i Christum Filium tuum Qui tecum`; the 1862 sets 14 point(s) of punctuation in this oration where the 1962 sets 11; the 1922 Mame reads `Postcommunio G iene` where the 1962 reads `Sacro`; the 1922 Mame reads `supplices` where the 1962 reads `siipplices` (letterforms inferred, not read: the difference is at the level of the recogniser); the 1922 Mame reads `tuze` where the 1962 reads `tuae` (letterforms inferred, not read: the difference is at the level of the recogniser); 4 further place(s) differ only in orthography, ligature or the recogniser's letterforms; the 1922 Mame prints the conclusion as `Per Dominum DIE 17 APRILIS SANCTI ANICETI PAP ET MART Missa Protexisti` where the 1962 prints `Per Dominum nostrum Iesum i Christum Filium tuum Qui tecum`. Corroboration: 1922 Tours Mame, printed p. 570 (artifact PDF p. 684), target-body character coverage 0.92, found by a sweep; Benziger 1962 conformed printing, target-body character coverage 0.90. Recorded limitation: The 1922 Mame likewise files these words at a place of its own rather than under this day. Every 1862 reading here rests on that book's whole-book text layer alone; this lane has no page image of the 1862, and the recogniser damages roughly one word in three there, so where the 1862's letterforms differ from the 1962's the difference recorded above is an inference from the layer and not a reading of the leaf. The 1922 Mame is the check on those places, and it is a full public-domain peer rather than mere corroboration. Not checked: the 1962 page image for this oration, the 1570 (its recogniser is too degraded to control a claim), and the 1604 except where named. || REPAIRED by lane repair-2 on 2026-09-03. The stored target had been a text-layer reading carrying recogniser damage; it has been replaced word for word by a reading taken from the 1962 CMAA facsimile page image at 400 dpi (artifact PDF p. 588, printed folio read on the same image). Line-end hyphens are joined, printed stress accents are dropped, and the ae/oe ligatures are expanded to two letters; punctuation, capitalisation and the conclusion are reproduced at the length the page prints them. The verdict, the antecedent locus and the recorded differences are the original lane's and were not revisited. The marginal number 2415 already in the locus was confirmed on the same 400 dpi image; it stands in the left-hand column under the rubric Pro Ss. Martyribus / Postcommunio. NOTE FOR THE REVIEWER, not a change to this entry: the same prayer is printed again at no. 2418 in the right-hand column of the same page, in the Eodem die 14 aprilis commemoration block from which this mass's Collect (no. 2416) was taken, and there it ends with the short conclusion cue instead of the written-out one. The originating lane collated the no. 2415 form, which is what is reproduced here; the word-level text of the two is otherwise the same. The stored string also carried several stray tokens picked up from the right-hand column's marginal numbers bleeding into the text layer, which is why its word count ran five above the printed oration's; those are gone from the page reading.

propers.name: Postcommunion
propers.text:
Sacro munere satiati, supplices te, Domine, deprecamur: ut, quod debitae
servitutis celebramus officio, salvationis tuae sentiamus augmentum. Per
Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum, Filium tuum: Qui tecum.
